P.flaw: Belly hatch is a plain brass rectangle on a stubby pole end, so the hatch and the pole as sole support read weakly from below.

Q.flaw: The hatch is filled faded red with a brass frame rather than a charcoal rectangle on the plate, and the pole pokes out below the belly.

R.flaw: The tail is ivory and blends into the body, so the swept tail wedge is weak.

S.flaw: The head is thin and the legs are spindly with a very small pole stub, so the horse looks less chunky and the pole barely reads from below.

model-1.why_top: Q meets all limits and has the clearest belly hatch with a visible brass frame, a continuous pole and a readable forward-facing head.

P.flaw: The lamp hangs below and in front of the pivot rather than just behind it.

Q.flaw: The lamp is partly hidden behind the arm and overlaps the pivot boss.

R.flaw: The footing and post are shrunk to 0.37 m deep and offset, so the model is off-centre and the lamp is small and under the arm.

S.flaw: The lamp housing sits behind the post and is almost hidden from the front, so its position is hard to read.

model-2.why_top: Q shows the 45 degree raised arm, the pivot boss, the lamp and the counterweight clearly from the front within the size and triangle limits.
